title: Plant-Environment Measurement & Crop Response
level: Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners entering the Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist pathway
Cultivation personnel responsible for crop-environment measurement, sensor interpretation, spatial mapping and evidence-based environmental handoff
prerequisites: Cultivation Technician II environmental/sensor competency or equivalent measurement foundation
evidencePolicy: Plant-environment relationships are grounded in cannabis-specific peer-reviewed evidence plus university protected-environment measurement and lighting guidance. Research treatment values, greenhouse examples and cultivar-specific responses are not converted into universal cannabis room targets without facility validation.
assessmentPolicy: The dedicated specialist assessment is development-only until exact-version technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize HVAC, electrical, controls, gas, calibration or environmental setpoint changes outside assigned authority.
description: Develops specialist measurement and interpretation of the crop environment, emphasizing representative sensor placement, spatial and temporal gradients, temperature/RH/VPD relationships, leaf-versus-air conditions, radiation/light context, crop response, data quality and evidence-based escalation.
learningOutcomes: Design a representative environmental measurement plan that accounts for sensor placement, shielding, crop zone, spatial gradients, time-series behavior and calibration/verification status.
Interpret temperature and relative humidity together through vapor-pressure and dew-point concepts while distinguishing room-air conditions from leaf-surface conditions.
Relate PPFD, photoperiod and DLI measurements to crop-environment context without converting examples from other crops or studies into universal cannabis targets.
Analyze crop response alongside environmental measurements to distinguish true room events, local microclimates, sensor error and plant-specific conditions.
Produce a reconstructable environmental verification report that states measurement quality, observed pattern, confidence, limits, permitted action and escalation needs.
